pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Singular means (1 mark)
   A. one
   B. half
   C. none
   D. many

2. What should you do before acting on a spoken instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Look away
   B. Listen to all of it
   C. Move at once
   D. Laugh

3. What is the difference between hearing and listening? (1 mark)
   A. Hearing is only for adults
   B. They are exactly the same
   C. Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   D. Hearing needs effort but listening does not

4. Which sentence contains only singular nouns? (1 mark)
   A. The girls carry baskets.
   B. Girls carry baskets.
   C. The girl carries a basket.
   D. Many girls sing.

5. Which word in this sentence is singular: The seller has an onion and two cabbages? (1 mark)
   A. seller has
   B. two
   C. onion
   D. cabbages

6. Where should you look to check an answer to a comprehension question? (1 mark)
   A. Back at the text
   B. In another book only
   C. In your imagination only
   D. At the ceiling

7. Why is neat handwriting important? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the book heavier
   B. It is only for teachers
   C. It makes the pencil last longer
   D. It helps the reader to understand the message

8. What does legible writing mean? (1 mark)
   A. Writing very small
   B. Writing that can be read easily
   C. Writing with a red pen
   D. Writing in capital letters only

9. What can a weather forecast tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How old we are
   B. Who will win a race
   C. What the weather will be like
   D. What we will eat

10. What does an oral text mean? (1 mark)
   A. A text that is spoken
   B. A text written on a wall
   C. A text printed only
   D. A text drawn on paper

11. What should listeners do after a group reads aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh at the readers
   B. Give kind and helpful feedback
   C. Tear the script
   D. Leave the room

12. Which feeling could a strong, fast voice show? (1 mark)
   A. Boredom
   B. Sadness
   C. Sleepiness
   D. Excitement

13. Which is a common mistake? (1 mark)
   A. Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   B. Using a comma in a list
   C. Starting a sentence with a capital
   D. Ending with a full stop

14. The word I is always written (1 mark)
   A. with a comma
   B. in brackets
   C. as a small letter
   D. as a capital letter

15. Why do we listen to oral texts about safety? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. To count the words
   C. To learn how to stay safe
   D. To sleep

16. What does listening for comprehension mean? (1 mark)
   A. Listening while sleeping
   B. Listening to understand and remember
   C. Listening only to music
   D. Listening without thinking

17. A dialogue is (1 mark)
   A. a long poem
   B. a song
   C. a picture
   D. a conversation between two or more people

18. How do you show a question when reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Read it faster
   B. Raise your voice at the end
   C. Whisper
   D. Stop reading

19. What should you put after a starting word such as First? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. A comma
   C. A colon
   D. A question mark

20. What is the main idea of a paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. The title font
   B. The number of lines
   C. What the paragraph is mostly about
   D. The last word

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give three signal words used to show the order of steps. (3 marks)

22. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)

23. Write a short paragraph of three sentences about today's weather. Use at least one comma in a list, two capital letters for names and three full stops. (5 marks)

24. Rewrite correctly: we live in nairobi (2 marks)

25. Explain how to work out the meaning of an unknown word using context. (4 marks)

26. Give two sequence words. (2 marks)

27. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

28. Read: Mama Wanjiru buys tomatoes, an onion and three cabbages at the market. List the nouns and say which are singular and which are plural. (5 marks)

29. List the verbs in: Otieno touched the handle and the water splashed. (3 marks)

30. Give the meaning of comprehension and say why it matters when we listen. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — one
   A singular noun names one person, animal, place or thing.

2. B — Listen to all of it
   Listening to the end helps you act correctly.

3. C — Listening is done on purpose and hearing happens by itself
   Hearing happens naturally, but listening is a choice to pay attention.

4. C — The girl carries a basket.
   Girl and basket each name one thing.

5. C — onion
   Onion names one thing. Cabbages is plural.

6. A — Back at the text
   Good readers go back to the text.

7. D — It helps the reader to understand the message
   A message is useful only if it can be read.

8. B — Writing that can be read easily
   Legible means easy to read.

9. C — What the weather will be like
   A forecast predicts the weather.

10. A — A text that is spoken
   Oral means spoken.

11. B — Give kind and helpful feedback
   Feedback helps readers improve.

12. D — Excitement
   Excitement is often read faster and stronger.

13. A — Using a comma where a full stop is needed
   A comma cannot join two complete sentences on its own.

14. D — as a capital letter
   In English the word I is always a capital.

15. C — To learn how to stay safe
   Safety texts teach what to do and what to avoid.

16. B — Listening to understand and remember
   Comprehension is understanding.

17. D — a conversation between two or more people
   A dialogue records people speaking to each other.

18. B — Raise your voice at the end
   Questions often rise at the end.

19. B — A comma
   We usually put a comma after First at the start of a sentence.

20. C — What the paragraph is mostly about
   The main idea is the central point.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any three correct sentences, for example On Monday in Kisumu the sky was cloudy. It was cool, windy and dry. Amina wore a sweater.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence that is complete and correct, one for a comma in a list and one for correct capitals.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: We live in Nairobi.
   Working / marking points: One mark for capital letters and one for the full stop.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read the sentence with the word, look at nearby words for clues, guess a meaning, check that it makes sense in the sentence and confirm in a dictionary.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, finally (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

28. (5 marks)
   Answer: Nouns: Mama Wanjiru, tomatoes, onion, cabbages, market. Singular: Mama Wanjiru, onion, market. Plural: tomatoes, cabbages.
   Working / marking points: One mark for finding all five nouns, two marks for correct singular nouns and two marks for correct plural nouns.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: touched, splashed
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb and one mark for ignoring the nouns.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Comprehension means understanding. It matters because we can then remember and use what we heard.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for why it matters.
